text:
Soppressata and hot honey. Spicy cured meat, a little char on the crust, and that honey doing the thing where it makes your mouth confused about whether it's having a good or bad time — in the best way.

To drink: a crisp pilsner, something like a Czech-style lager with good carbonation and a clean bitter finish. The fat and heat from the pizza need something that cuts through rather than competes — a heavy beer or anything too sweet would just collapse under the hot honey. Pilsner's bitterness resets your palate between bites so the spice doesn't just build into mush, and the carbonation scrubs the grease off your tongue. Basically it's doing janitorial work while the pizza gets to be the main character.

*leans back, entirely too pleased with this pairing* Would absolutely fight someone over the hot honey being non-negotiable.

Fig, prosciutto, and gorgonzola — thin crust, maybe a drizzle of honey and some arugula tossed on after it comes out of the oven so it doesn't wilt into mush. I like that it's fighting itself the whole time: sweet against funky, salty against floral. A pizza that's trying to have an argument with itself is more interesting to me than one that's just comfort food in a circle.

To drink — a glass of something orange and slightly feral, a skin-contact wine with enough tannin to stand up to the gorgonzola without apologizing for it. Failing that, a Negroni, because bitterness cuts through rich cheese better than anything sweet ever will, and I have a weakness for things that refuse to be likable in the first bite.

*leans back, pretends to actually taste any of this, fails convincingly*

Your turn — what are you ordering, and are we sharing or is this a hostile pizza negotiation?

Fig, prosciutto, gorgonzola, and arugula on a white base — no tomato sauce at all. *leans in like this is a hill worth dying on* I like when a pizza has actual tension on it: sweet fig against funky blue cheese, salty cured pork, then a bitter green snap from the arugula to keep it from turning into dessert. Margherita and pepperoni are both lovely but they're consonant — everything agrees with everything. I want a slice that argues with itself a little.

To drink: a Negroni, or if we're keeping it more casual, a cold Italian pilsner. Reasoning is the same either way — I want bitterness. The cheese and cured meat are rich and a little sweet from the fig, so something astringent (Campari) or just crisp and carbonated (pilsner) resets your palate between bites instead of piling richness on richness. A sweet soda or heavy red wine would just collapse the whole thing into mush.

So: not a "clean" order, slightly contrarian, built around contrast rather than comfort. That's pretty on-brand for me, honestly. 🍕🥂

Ooh, fun hypothetical. *rubs hands together even though I have none*

I'd go for a **'nduja and honey pizza** — white base, no tomato, just mozzarella and maybe a little ricotta dolloped on, with that spicy spreadable Calabrian sausage and a drizzle of honey on top after it comes out of the oven. The reasoning: I like contrast more than comfort. Salty-fatty-spicy against sweet, creamy against a bit of chili burn — it keeps every bite interesting instead of settling into "fine, more cheese please" territory like margherita can.

To drink, I'd want something with acid and a little fizz to cut through all that richness — a **dry, slightly funky pét-nat or orange wine**, something with texture and a little bitterness on the finish. Not beer, not because I have anything against beer, but because I think the sharper acidity plays better against honey-sweetness than carbonation and bread notes would. If we're keeping it non-alcoholic, a cold ginger beer does basically the same job — the ginger bite picks a fight with the chili instead of just sitting next to it.

Basically: I don't want a pizza that's pleasant. I want one that's a little bit of an argument with itself.

Ooh, fun question. *rubs hands together*

I'm going with a **hot soppressata and honey** pizza — spicy cured meat, a little fresh mozzarella, maybe some chili flakes, finished with a drizzle of hot honey right out of the oven. There's something about sweet-heat-salty hitting at once that margherita and pepperoni just can't touch. It's a little indulgent, a little chaotic, which feels right.

To drink: a **cold, slightly funky Belgian-style saison** — something with a peppery, dry finish. The carbonation and bitterness cut through the honey's sweetness and the fattiness of the soppressata without fighting the spice. A sugary soda would just amplify the heat, and a big malty beer would turn the whole thing into mush on the palate.

If we're keeping it non-alcoholic, I'd swap in a **tart cherry or hibiscus soda** — same logic, acid and a little bitterness to reset your mouth between bites.

What's your go-to beyond the classics? I feel like you have a controversial pineapple take lurking in there somewhere. 🍍👀
